questions.question: What does Michał finish after five years of work?
questions.explanation: After five years the algorithm is ready.

questions.question: What does Ewa say about Dostoyevsky's protagonist?
answers: That he would do something to ruin his own mood — out of contrariness
questions.explanation: Ewa asks about the man who would spoil his mood out of contrariness.

questions.question: What does Ewa say the algorithm would describe about the tree?
answers: The species, age and height — but not what Michał sees
questions.explanation: She says the algorithm would give the maple, 120 years, 15 metres — but not the experience.

questions.question: What does Michał see when he looks at the tree with his eyes closed?
answers: The snow and that he is with Ewa
questions.explanation: He says: I see the snow and that I'm here with you.

questions.question: What does Michał do with the algorithm at the end?
answers: He deletes the modules that suggest changes — he leaves only information gathering
He hands it to the team
questions.explanation: He deletes the modules that propose changes; he leaves a simple information tool.
